2065.subject: Zoology
2065.text: Which of the following are uricotelic animals?
2065.sol: Uricotelic animals (living in dry conditions) are those animals which excrete uric acid as their excretory product e.g. lizard and crow. These animals conserve water in their bodies and synthesize crystals of uric acids from ammonia. These crystals can be retained in the body (in solid form) for a considerable time before being discharged from the body.

2190.subject: Zoology
2190.text: Examine the diagram of the two cell types A and B given below and select the correct option
options: Cell A is the rod cell found evenly all over retina
Cell A is the cone cell more concentrated in the fovea centralis
Cell B is concerned with colour vision in bright light
Cell A is sensitive to low light intensities
2190.sol: Cone cell is one of two types (other is rod) of light sensitive cells in the retina of the eye. The human retina contains 6-7 million cones which function best in bright light and are essential for active vision (receiving a sharp accurate image). The area of retina called the fovea contains the greatest concentration of cone. Cones can also distinguish colours. There are 3 types of cone, each sensitive to the wavelength of a different primary colour - red, green or blue.

4186.subject: Chemistry
4186.text: Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity for nucleophilic addition reaction
4186.sol: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions due to steric and electronic reasons. Sterically, the presence of two relatively large substituents in ketones hinders the approach of nucleophile to carbonyl carbon than in aldehydes having only one such substituent. Electronically, aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because two alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more effectively than in former. Benzophenone being a ketone is the least reactive

42499.subject: Physics
42499.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : For all elements, greater the mass of the nucleus, greater is the binding energy per nucleon. Statement II : For all elements, nuclei with less binding energy per nucleon transforms to nuclei with greater binding energy per nucleon. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
42499.sol: Statement I is false because binding energy per nucleon does not increase monotonically with mass number. It peaks at Iron-56 and decreases for heavier elements. Statement II is true. It describes the fundamental principle of nuclear reactions: fission of heavy nuclei (low BE/A) and fusion of light nuclei (low BE/A) both produce nuclei with higher binding energy per nucleon, releasing energy in the process. Both processes are energetically favorable for the same reason: moving toward higher stability (higher BE/A).

68451.text: Two bodies A and B move in same straight line starting from same position. Body A moves with constant velocity 'u' and body B moves with constant acceleration ' a '. When their velocities become equal, the distance between them is

71217.subject: Biology
71217.text: The biofertilizer ________ supplies nitrogen and antibiotics into the soil.
71217.sol: Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium present in the soil. Along with fixing atmospheric nitrogen, it also produces certain antibiotics and plant growth substances (like vitamins and hormones) that enhance soil fertility and inhibit the growth of pathogenic microorganisms. Answer: Azotobacter

71220.subject: Biology
71220.text: Which one of the following biofertilizer makes the plant associated with them grow luxuriantly in less irrigated lands?
71220.sol: Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhizae (VAM) are symbiotic associations between fungi and the roots of higher plants. The fungal hyphae extend into the soil, significantly increasing the surface area for absorption. This allows the plant to absorb water and essential nutrients, particularly phosphorus, more efficiently from the soil. Due to this enhanced water uptake capability, plants associated with VAM can grow luxuriantly even in less irrigated or drought-prone lands. Answer: Vesiculo Arbuscular Mycorrhizae

As a result, the embryos are genetically identical to the parent plant, ensuring the preservation of desirable traits (clonal propagation). 105609.text: The work functions of four metals P, Q, R and S are 2.1 eV, 2.8 eV, 3.4 eV and 4.5 eV respectively. If monochromatic light of wavelength 400 nm is incident on each of them, which of these metals will exhibit photoelectric emission? (Take hc = 1240 eV nm)
105609.sol: The energy of an incident photon is given by E = hc . Substituting the given values: E = 1240 eV nm 400 nm = 3.1 eV . For photoelectric emission to occur, the energy of the incident photon must be greater than or equal to the work function of the metal ( E ). Comparing the incident photon energy ( E = 3.1 eV ) with the given work functions: For P: 3.1 eV > 2.1 eV (Emission occurs) For Q: 3.1 eV > 2.8 eV (Emission occurs) For R: 3.1 eV For S: 3.1 eV Therefore, only metals P and Q will exhibit photoelectric emission.

127139.subject: Botany
127139.text: How many plant and animal species have been described so far according to IUCN (2004)?
127139.sol: Since there are published records of all the species discovered and named, we know how many species in all have been recorded so far, but it is not easy to answer the question of how many species there are on earth. According to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) (2004), the total number of plant and animal species described so far is slightly more than 1.5 million, but we have no clear idea of how many species are yet to be discovered and described. 127144.subject: Botany
127144.text: Out of every 10 animals on earth, how many are insects?
127144.sol: More than 70 per cent of all the species recorded are animals, while plants (including algae, fungi, bryophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms) comprise no more than 22 per cent of the total. Among animals, insects are the most species-rich taxonomic group, making up more than 70 per cent of the total. That means, out of every 10 animals on this planet, 7 are insects. 127248.subject: Botany
127248.text: How is India contributing to biodiversity conservation?
127248.sol: Biodiversity conservation may be in situ as well as ex situ. In in situ conservation, the endangered species are protected in their natural habitat so that the entire ecosystem is protected. Recently, 34 ‘biodiversity hotspots’ in the world have been proposed for intensive conservation efforts. Of these, three (Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Himalaya and Indo-Burma) cover India’s rich biodiversity regions. Our country’s in situ conservation efforts are reflected in its 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, > 450 wild

127444.text: The World Summit on sustainable development held in 2002 in Johannesburg, South Africa pledged for:
options: A significant reduction in the current rate of biodiversity loss.
Collection and preservation of seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants.
127444.sol: World summit on sustainable development takes place to ensure significant reduction in the current rate of Biodiversity loss. This summit was held in 2002 in Johannerburg, South Africa.

127509.subject: Botany
127509.text: Biodiversity act of India was passed by the Parliament in the year.
127509.sol: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 is an Act enacted by the Parliament of India for the preservation of biological diversity in India, and provides mechanism for equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of traditional biological resources and knowledge.

127526.subject: Botany

people are an integral part of the system

living organisms are brought from all over the world and preserved for posterity.
127526.sol: Biosphere reserves, National Park and wild life sanctuaries are all protected areas but differ from each other in some ways. National parks are reserved for betterment of wild life. Cultivation, grazing forestry and habitat manipulations are not allowed. Sanctuaries are tracts of land with or with out lake where wild life can take refuge without being hunted. Blood from the glomerulus is carried away by an efferent arteriole. The renal tubule begins with a double walled cup-like structure called Bowman’s capsule, which encloses the glomerulus. Z-line 3 .Structural unit composed of actin and myosin filaments D. H-zone 4. Defines the boundary of a sarcomere
130397.sol: Sarcomere: The basic functional unit of muscle contraction, extending from one Z-line to the next. Myofibril: Composed of repeating units of sarcomeres, made up of actin and myosin filaments. Z-line: The boundary of a sarcomere, where actin filaments are anchored. H-zone: A region in the A-band that contains only thick filaments and appears lighter.

95180.subject: Botany
95180.text: Viral infection is usually absent in
95180.sol: The apical meristems are present in the apices of primary and secondary shoots and roots of the plant. The cells of apical meristem are in an active stage of division, have dense cytoplasm, thin cell wall, and remain virus-free. Due to this reason, meristematic culture is carried out to obtain virus-free plants.

95754.subject: Botany
options: The cell envelope consists of a tightly bound three layered structure, of which plasma membrane is the innermo
A specialised differentiated form of cell membrane called mesosome is the characteristic of prokaryotes.
Surface structures of the bacteria, like flagella, pili and fimbriae play a major role in motility.
Gas vacuoles are found in blue green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.
95754.sol: Besides flagella, Pili and Fimbriae are also surface structures of the bacteria but do not play a role in motility. The pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein. The fimbriae are small bristle like fibres sprouting out of the cell. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.

95776.subject: Botany
95776.text: Select the organism that cannot make food with light as source of energy.
95776.sol: Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan which is parasitic in nature. It causes diseases like Sleeping sickness. Gonyaulax is a photosynthetic dinoflagellate. Chlamydomonas is a single celled alga. Nostoc is a photosynthetic cyanobacterium.

95942.subject: Botany
95942.text: In nature, a symbiotic association is found between an algae and a fungus. Which of the following can be regarded as the correct property for this association?
options: Lichens are fast growing organisms that live for a short period
The algal component is called mycobiont and fungal component is called phycobiont
They are pioneers of vegetation on rocks.
95942.sol: Lichens are symbiotic associations between algae and fungi. The autotrophic algal component is called phycobiont and the heterotrophic fungal component is called as mycobiont. Algae prepare food for fungi and fungi provide shelter and absorb mineral nutrients and water for its partner. Lichens are very good pollution indicators - they do not grow in polluted areas and in cities. Lichens are pioneers in the xerosere type of ecological succession on barren rocks.

96119.sol: DNA is wrapped histone proteins to form beads like structure called nucleosomes. This structure is further condensed to fit in a coiled helical structure called solenoid that on folding forms the chromatin fibre. Nucleosome forms the structural unit of chromatin fibre. Microtubules found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells are made of polymers of protein, tubulin. Microtubules help with the structure and shape of the cell. Tight junctions are a type of cell junctions found in epithelial tissue that help to stop su

96136.subject: Botany
96136.text: Detailed membrane structure was studied only after the advent of ________
96136.sol: The detailed structure of the membrane was studied only after the advent of the electron microscope in the year 1950.

96607.subject: Botany
options: Carbon cycle is imperfect cycle while phosphorus cycle is perfect cycle.
Ten percent law was proposed by Odum in 1942.
Grazing food chain helps in releasing inorganic nutrients to the cycling pool.
Seral community is a transitional community which develops in an area during succession.
96607.sol: The process of the changes occurring in the structure of various organisms in an ecosystem over a period of time is referred to as ecological succession. During ecological succession, one of the intermediate stages that develops is called the seral community. It gets replaced by a successive community during the succession process. 97044.sol: When stamens are attached to petals then it is called an epipetalous condition. Epipetalous stamens are present in members of Solanaceae family like tomato, petunia, tobacco, and chilli.

97170.subject: Botany
97170.sol: Search for natural substances with cytokinin-like activities led to the isolation of zeatin from corn-kernels and coconut milk. For the first time, zeatin was obtained from corn milk by Letham in 1963.

97215.subject: Botany
97215.text: Respiratory climactic is brought about by which of the following hormones?
97215.sol: Ethylene is highly effective in fruit ripening. It enhances the respiration rate during the ripening of the fruits. This rise in the rate of respiration is called respiratory climactic.

97366.subject: Botany
97366.text: Plant growth hormones extracted from a fungus and a fish are respectively
97366.sol: Gibberellins is the plant hormone that was produced from the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi after isolation and therefore the fungus is named gibberellin. This hormone is a plant growth regulator and is involved in stem elongation, dormancy, and various other processes involving plant growth. Kinetin is also a plant hormone that helps in plant growth by promoting cell division. This hormone was first isolated from the DNA of herring fish.

97870.subject: Botany
97870.text: What is the correct order in decreasing size in taxonomic hierarchy?
options: Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species.
Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, species and genus.
Kingdom, phylum, class, species, order, family and genus.

97870.sol: Taxonomy is the branch of biological science which includes nomenclature and classification of the organisms into groups based on their shared features and characteristics. 309307.text: Which of the following statements about the pyranose form of mannose is incorrect ?

304209.text: A wave pulse travels on a string towards the positive X -axis with a speed v . At t = 0 , the shape of the string is given by g(x) = A (x/a) , where A and a are constants. Determine the dimensions of A and a .
304209.sol: The displacement of the string g(x) has the dimension of length, so [g(x)] = [L] . From the given equation g(x) = A (x/a) , the amplitude A must have the same dimension as g(x) . Therefore, [A] = [L] . The argument of the trigonometric function must be dimensionless. Thus, [x/a] = [M^0 L^0 T^0] . Since x represents position, [x] = [L] . Therefore, [a] = [x] = [L] . 303620.text: A point source is located at a depth h beneath the surface of water (refractive index = ). Identify the shape of the area on the water surface through which light escapes, along with the position of its centre.
options: A circular area with its centre directly above the point source
A rectangular area with its centre directly above the point source
A circular area whose centre is shifted horizontally by a distance h
An elliptical area with its centre directly above the point source
303620.sol: Light rays from the point source at depth h will escape the water surface if their angle of incidence at the water-air interface is less than or equal to the critical angle _c . The critical angle is given by _c = 1 . By symmetry, the locus of all points on the surface where the angle of incidence is exactly _c is a circle. The radius of this circle is r = h _c = h ^2 - 1 . Thus, the light escapes through a circular area on the water surface. The centre of this circular area lies directly above the point source.

305813.subject: Physics
305813.text: Determine the change in the internal energy of a gas confined in a rigid container when 100 J of heat is provided to it.
305813.sol: For a rigid container, the volume of the gas remains constant, so V = 0 . The work done by the gas is W = P V = 0 . According to the first law of thermodynamics, Q = U + W . Given that the heat provided to the gas is Q = 100 J . Substituting the values, 100 = U + 0 . Therefore, the change in internal energy is U = 100 J .

options: increase the concentration of S ²⁻ ions for faster precipitation
increase the concentration of Cl ⁻ ions to form soluble chloride complexes
dissolve any interfering phosphate ions present in the mixture
decrease the concentration of S ²⁻ ions by common ion effect
6a7a1ff8c3b227f6738e85eb.sol: HCl is a strong acid that completely dissociates to give H ⁺ and Cl ⁻ ions.
